Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

hvtiRdatabuild 0.3.6

  • New interim tools for correcting warehouse source views, superseded by the HVTR registry: generate_corrections_sql() writes each declared source’s corrections tables and its corrected, applied, stale and conflicts views, covering every column; write_corrections_template(), propose_corrections() and decide_corrections() take a whole submission and refuse it whole if any row fails, with a verdict per row and no values in any message; retire_filled_corrections() retires fill-ins upstream has caught up with; and study_correction_candidates() turns a study’s own fixes into candidate corrections against its frozen pull. In these views, accepted corrections to one cell that disagree do not resolve to the latest: neither applies until one is superseded.

  • read_master_config() reads sources (correctable source views and their keys) and deciders from master.yml.

  • On SQL Server, table_types() now carries a decimal column’s precision and scale, so the master corrections view built by lift_master() no longer casts to a bare decimal, which SQL Server reads as decimal(18,0) and rounds.

  • parse_value() now parses logical columns.

  • propose_corrections() now checks that each key survives the warehouse’s cast to its key column unchanged, as it already did for values. Before, an integer key 1.2 loaded as 1, so a correction could name, and after acceptance change, a different row. Such a key is now unknown_key. A submitted date, timestamp or number must also be the whole of its supported form (YYYY-MM-DD, that plus HH:MM[:SS[.fff]], or a plain decimal): 2020-01-01junk was read as 2020-01-01 and could name that row, and 0x23 was read as 35. Such a key is unknown_key and such a value does_not_cast.

  • study_correction_candidates() refuses a missing key in the pull or in data (missing_key); before, a missing key read as the text "NA" and could match a real key of that value. Its composite keys are now collision-safe, whatever the values contain.

  • propose_corrections(), decide_corrections(), retire_filled_corrections(), study_correction_candidates() and read_pull_provenance() now have examples that run, on synthetic data in DuckDB: a whole propose, decide and retire round trip, and a study fix turned into a candidate correction. Their examples were comments only.

hvtiRdatabuild 0.3.5

  • New pull_master() selects a cohort and reads its rows from a master view in one snapshot-isolation transaction, joined through a session temp table, and records the SQL commit, the ids of the corrections applied and the study configuration’s checksum. It refuses a master that has not passed its parity gate at the deployed SQL commit. cohort_query() defines a cohort by query, epoch and index ("first" or "all"), computed in the database, with a qualifying encounter before the epoch recorded as a counted stage. build_from_master() turns the pull into the build_result that derive_vars() consumes. freeze_study_pull() publishes the pull as a parquet release carrying its provenance in the file, read back with read_pull_provenance(), and refuses a study configuration changed since the pull.

  • New cohort_unit_id() and split_cohort_unit() key a cohort by MRN and encounter date, so a patient with two operations is two units.

  • publish_dataset() accepts .parquet drafts.

  • snapshot_master() compares the source SAS file’s sha256 with the one its sidecar records, and snapshots a rebuilt current master again instead of skipping it. lift_master() refuses a snapshot whose current build has changed since it was taken.

  • lift_master() names the base table for the snapshot’s release and the first 12 hex digits of its sha256, and the load log records the parquet’s sha256 with each row group. Re-lifting a rebuilt master loads a new base table and moves the view to it, where it used to skip the row groups already logged. A load log written for a different parquet now stops the load.

  • publish_dataset() on bytes identical to a withdrawn release is an error that names the withdrawn release and says how to reinstate it. It used to return the withdrawn record as if publication had worked.

  • write_analysis_set() counts each event code explicitly: n_censored (0), n_events (1), n_other_events (any other code) and n_event_missing (NA). n_censored was n minus the events, which counted competing risks and missing codes as censored. expect: accepts the two new counts.

  • A patient whose value is NA on an exclusion rule is still kept, for SAS parity, and is now counted at each rule they reach in a new attrition column, n_na_kept.

  • write_analysis_set() holds the study’s manifest lock while it writes, and the sidecar records the parquet’s sha256. read_analysis_set() stops when the sidecar does not describe the parquet beside it. A sidecar written before this change is not checked until the set is rewritten.

  • compare_built() matches numeric ids by value: a double 100000 in a SAS oracle and an integer 100000L in R no longer show up as row drift.

  • dw_connect() defaults to trust_certificate = FALSE, so the warehouse server’s TLS certificate is checked. A failed connection that checked it says how to install the CA chain, and that trust_certificate = TRUE is a stop-gap only.

  • The analysis-set examples call hvtiRutilities::register_data(file = , root = ), and exclusions pass patient_id_col to hvtiPlotR::hv_consort_start().

  • compare_built() writes numeric ids losslessly, so two distinct doubles never become one id, and it refuses whole-number ids beyond 2^53, which a double cannot hold exactly.

  • read_analysis_set() holds the study’s manifest lock, shared, while it verifies the sidecar, the manifest entry and the parquet’s hash and reads the parquet, so a writer cannot replace the parquet between the check and the read.

  • Informational messages go through the hvtiR family’s quiet mode: options(hvti.quiet = TRUE) silences them. Warnings and errors are never silenced.

  • Quiet mode cannot hide unfinished work. snapshot_master() warns, with class hvtiRdatabuild_snapshot_failed, when a historical snapshot fails, naming the files. backfill_corrections() warns, with class hvtiRdatabuild_incomplete_backfill, when a legacy fact is unresolved or a statement unparsed, giving counts and program line numbers only. Its result gains unparsed, unresolved_lines and unparsed_lines.

  • Errors a caller is expected to catch carry an hvtiRdatabuild_<condition> class and hvtiRdatabuild_error: withdrawn_release, stale_snapshot, parity_failed, key_not_unique, load_log_mismatch, parity_gate, connection_failed, lock_timeout, unregistered_parent, expect_failed, analysis_set_not_written, analysis_set_integrity, stale_analysis_set and both_names. Their messages start with the function’s name.

  • The stale-analysis-set message carries hvtiRdatabuild_stale_analysis_set first and hvtiRutilities_stale_analysis_set second. The old class goes in the next release.

  • pull_master() returns $meta, which leads with the hvtiR provenance record (package, version, sha, method, seed, rng_kind, time). $provenance is deprecated and goes in the next release. The analysis-set sidecar carries the same record, and its written time is ISO 8601 local time with its UTC offset, which as.POSIXct() reads back.

  • Renamed arguments, each deprecated for one release with a once-per-session warning of class hvtiRdatabuild_deprecated. Giving both the old and the new name is an error that names both.

    • compare_built(id) is id_col, with no default ("ccfidu" was one study’s column).
    • parse_legacy_facts(key_var) is key_col, with no default.
    • pull_master(columns, study_config) are var_cols and path.
    • propose_correction(variable) is var_col.
    • snapshot_master(out_dir) is dir, and so is datasets_dir in publish_dataset(), withdraw_dataset_release() and freeze_study_pull().
    • freeze_study_pull(study_config) is path.
    • snapshot_oracle(sas_path, out_path) are path and file.
    • dw_pull(conn) is con.

  • A failed dw_connect() now says what failed, in its message and in the error’s kind field: the driver or DSN would not load, the server could not be reached (DNS or route), the TLS handshake failed, or the login was refused. The certificate advice appears only where a certificate can be the cause. The driver’s own message is still never shown.

  • cohort_query() takes criteria: inclusion and exclusion criteria evaluated in the warehouse inside pull_master()’s transaction, each a counted cohort stage. A criterion (criterion()) wraps a test: master_row(), view_rows() (rows of another view in a day window, judged by pick = "any", "all" or "nearest"), or any_of() / all_of(). Only keys and flags leave the database.

  • No clinical defaults: role, undetermined, window, pick, date_col and, with index = "first", index_on are required. index_on = "eligible" lets a patient’s later encounter be the index when an earlier one is excluded.

  • A unit a criterion cannot decide follows its undetermined route: exclude, keep, or chart review. review_criterion(), review_list() and apply_review() record review decisions from a checksummed file with declared reason codes, as review stages. build_from_master() and freeze_study_pull() refuse a pull awaiting review.

  • local_criterion() decides a criterion in R from a file outside the warehouse, after the snapshot, and records the file’s SHA-256.

  • review is a fourth cohort stage source.

  • pull_master() checks that every candidate unit matches one master row before any criterion runs, so a criterion can no longer filter a duplicate key out of sight.

  • After chart review moves a unit back to the criterion that routed it, apply_review() rebuilds each later criterion’s met, not met and undetermined tally from the units that reached it, so a stage’s provenance agrees with its counts. The figures evaluated at the pull are kept beside the tally, labelled, where they differ. pull_master() keeps each unit’s outcome at every warehouse and local criterion in review$outcomes.

  • A pull saved while awaiting review before review$outcomes existed cannot have its stages recounted. apply_review() refuses decisions that would change a counted stage on such a pull (hvtiRdatabuild_review_outcomes_missing); pull again with pull_master() and apply the decisions to the new pull. Decisions that change no counted stage are applied as before.

  • Documentation sweep before 0.3.5. apply_review() and review_list() gain a runnable example on synthetic data. The README’s status section lists the stages that ship, build_dataset() and derive_vars() among them, which it still called future work; it links vignette("master-datasets"), and says a stale analysis set is read with a note in a draft and refused in a final render. vignette("master-datasets") calls propose_correction(var_col =), so it no longer prints a deprecation warning, and points to pull_master() and build_from_master() for reading a master into a study. vignette("coming-from-sas") says compare_built() matches ids exactly, without trimming, and that a row whose exclude rule is NA is kept and counted in n_na_kept, with the rule to write when the SAS step deleted it.

hvtiRdatabuild 0.3.4

  • backfill_corrections(), propose_correction() and decide_correction() are deprecated. Corrections to master datasets move to the HVTR registry, and hvtiRdatabuild will read corrected data from it rather than record corrections itself. The functions still work and warn on every call with class deprecatedWarning; set options(hvtiRdatabuild.warn_deprecated_corrections = FALSE) to silence the warning (#101).

  • The write_analysis_set() and read_analysis_set() examples, and the test helper, call hvtiRutilities::register_data(file =) rather than the deprecated built =, so they no longer warn. The hvtiRutilities floor rises to 1.5.20, the first release with file =.

hvtiRdatabuild 0.3.3

  • write_analysis_set() builds a set from registered data only, because an analysis set is reused by other jobs. It refuses a working read of the study dataset, stops and writes nothing.
    • A dataset with no dated version, including one registered before dated versions (a manifest entry with no parquet), is refused before it is read and the message names hvtiRutilities::update_manifest(). Run it once to convert a legacy registration; sets already written read as before.
    • A registered dataset read as working because HVTI_DATA=working is set is refused with a message that says to unset HVTI_DATA.
    • In a final render or an Rscript run, hvtiRutilities’ own gate may refuse the read first, with its own message.
    • Requires hvtiRutilities 1.5.3, the first release that signals a working read.
  • The README points analysts to vignette("registered-datasets", package = "hvtiRutilities"), which explains dataset registration, version names and which version a job reads. It ships with hvtiRutilities 1.5.12 and later.

hvtiRdatabuild 0.3.2

  • The README’s Installation section now leads with hvtiR::install(), which installs the whole HVTI R family in one call, and then gives pak::pak("ehrlinger/hvtiRdatabuild") for this package alone.

  • Tests and examples pass renv and cleanup to hvtiRutilities::study_setup() explicitly, ahead of hvtiRutilities turning both on by default. A new test fails on any call that leaves them implicit.

  • The hvtiRutilities floor rises to 1.5.2, the first release whose study_setup() takes renv and cleanup.

hvtiRdatabuild 0.3.1

  • The test of an analysis set over a dataset registered before dated versions now writes the set as a datasets job would. hvtiRutilities’ stage gate serves a dataset with no dated version only to the console and to datasets or descriptive jobs, so the test’s non-interactive run was refused. Test-only.

hvtiRdatabuild 0.3.0

  • Now requires R 4.4.0 or newer, up from 4.1.0, to match the rest of the HVTI family. hvtiR::install() installs the members together, and several already required 4.4.0, so on an older R the install failed whatever this package declared. Now requires hvtiRutilities 1.5.1.

  • The build layer. Three pieces sit between dw_pull() and the analysis sets. build_dataset() joins a study’s patient-level modules on its cohort and keeps repeated-event tables beside the result rather than widening them. derive_vars() runs the study’s own R code, committed with the study, and takes back the data with an updated cohort. A cohort_record, from new_cohort_record(), append_cohort_stage() and cohort_summary(), carries inclusion, exclusion and attrition history through both, in order. A missing inclusion value is an error, not an implicit pass or exclusion. Duplicate source identifier columns are kept for audit, patient identifiers stay stable across joins, and the print() and str() methods and callback diagnostics never show a patient value. vignette("coming-from-sas") walks the build, study code and attrition through a synthetic example. dplyr moves from Suggests to Imports.

  • A stale analysis set no longer stops a draft. read_analysis_set() reads a set whose parent or declaration has changed, and signals hvtiRutilities_stale_analysis_set with the write_analysis_set() call that updates it. A final render (HVTI_TEMPLATE_STRICT set, as render_job(final = TRUE) does) still stops, with the same commands. This reverses the earlier rule that every stale read stopped; a damaged set still stops in every render.

  • An analysis set’s parent is now the registered version of the built dataset when hvtiRutilities registered it as a dated parquet. Rebuilding built.sas7bdat without registering it no longer makes every set stale, because jobs read nothing new until hvtiRutilities::update_manifest() registers it. Sets written before this change name the SAS file as their parent, so each is stale once after the study’s first update_manifest(); write_analysis_set() refreshes it. A dataset still registered the old way is identified by its source, as before.

  • write_analysis_set() and read_analysis_set() skip the line of text that hvtiRutilities 1.5.1 writes at the head of a manifest.yaml holding a registered dated version. Without this they stopped with “$ operator is invalid for atomic vectors” on every study registered from 1.5.1 on.

  • write_analysis_set() refuses a set named for a registered dated version, such as built_20261008, before writing anything. Its parquet would have replaced that version, the registered data every job reads.

  • DESCRIPTION now declares the Quarto command line tool in SystemRequirements. The vignettes have always needed it to build; the field makes that visible to installers and to R CMD check.

  • Articles on the pkgdown site put the table of contents on the left and use the full width of the window, through pkgdown/extra.css. The installed vignettes are unchanged: the Quarto vignette engine renders them in its own minimal format, which has no sidebar layout.

hvtiRdatabuild 0.2.4

  • Master datasets. Six new functions snapshot, lift and correct the master datasets that study builds read. read_master_config() reads a master.yml declaring a master’s key, alternate keys and parent. snapshot_master() freezes its SAS builds as parquet and records which parent release each was built from, read from the run’s log first. lift_master() loads a snapshot into the warehouse behind key and full-parity gates and creates the master’s view. backfill_corrections(), propose_correction() and decide_correction() keep an append-only record of corrections the view applies. The bulk functions dry-run by default. See vignette("master-datasets"). duckdb and tidyselect join Suggests.

  • An analysis set names its own event column. hvtiRutilities 1.4.0 made study registration endpoint-neutral: register_data() no longer takes event or time, and study_config() no longer carries a study-wide cohort. write_analysis_set() had counted n_events and n_censored from that cohort, so under 1.4.0 every write failed. A set now declares event: (one of its vars) to get both counts, and an expect on either count without one stops with a message naming the missing key. A set with no event records n alone. A set that relied on the study-wide cohort needs the one-line event: added, which also changes its declaration hash, so read_analysis_set() asks for one rewrite. hvtiRdatabuild now requires hvtiRutilities 1.4.0 or later, since its tests and registration fixture use the endpoint-neutral register_data().

  • snapshot_oracle() can snapshot a dataset too large for memory. The new chunk_rows argument reads the SAS dataset a chunk at a time and writes the chunks as row groups of one parquet file. It also records a SHA-256 of the SAS source beside the parquet checksum, and writes a .meta.json sidecar holding each column’s label, SAS format and type, so that metadata survives into systems that cannot read R attributes. jsonlite joins Suggests. The source checksum now brackets the read, taken before and after; a mismatch removes the parquet and stops rather than write a snapshot of a file that changed underneath it.

hvtiRdatabuild 0.2.3

  • New publish_dataset(). A programmer can publish a mutable clinical-data draft as an immutable dated release. Publication preserves the draft bytes, verifies that the staged copy is readable, records its checksum and shape in dataset-catalog.yml, and serializes concurrent publishers with a catalog lock. Same-day corrections receive revision filenames; retrying identical bytes is idempotent, including recovery of a file moved before a failed catalog write.

  • New withdraw_dataset_release(). Withdrawal records a reason and an optional replacement in the catalog without changing or deleting the published file. The package now requires hvtiRutilities 1.3.1, whose study workflow discovers, reviews, and explicitly adopts these releases.

hvtiRdatabuild 0.2.2

  • Documentation no longer points dw_pull() users at a building-a-study-dataset vignette that does not exist, and the SAS migration guide no longer lists the shipped dw_connect() and dw_pull() as future work. Prose across the README, vignette and reference pages was tightened.

  • The SAS migration guide now treats bd.SAStoR.sas outputs as general downstream data contracts rather than exports owned by their first consumer. It shows how the final selection becomes a shared analysis set while variable derivation remains in the build layer.

  • Analysis-set declarations now reject duplicate variables and require every expected row/event count to be one non-negative whole number. This prevents duplicate parquet columns from being silently renamed and fractional counts from matching after integer truncation.

  • Analysis sets resolve their outputs through the study’s logical datasets directory, preserving numbered new studies and adopted legacy layouts.

hvtiRdatabuild 0.2.1

  • New write_analysis_set() and read_analysis_set(). An analysis set is a declared, checkpointed selection of the built dataset: the columns a job reads and the rows it excludes, declared under analysis_sets: in _study.yml, written once to datasets/ as <name>.parquet with a sidecar recording its parent and per-rule attrition, and read by every job that needs it. Reading stops, rather than rebuilding, when the built dataset or the declaration has changed.

hvtiRdatabuild 0.2.0

Breaking Changes

  • Package renamed from hvtiRdatasets to hvtiRdatabuild. The package exports six functions and no data object, so a ...datasets name promised a payload and delivered a pipeline. Update library() calls and any hvtiRdatasets:: prefixes. The repository moved to github.com/ehrlinger/hvtiRdatabuild; GitHub redirects the old URL, so an existing remotes::install_github("ehrlinger/hvtiRdatasets") keeps resolving.
  • The print option hvtiRdatasets.show_ids is now hvtiRdatabuild.show_ids. There is no fallback to the old name: a stale options(hvtiRdatasets.show_ids = TRUE) is ignored and identifiers are not printed. That is the conservative direction for a flag whose own documentation warns it may emit PHI.

No function changed behaviour, so results are identical to 0.1.2.
